blocks.en: French verbs fall into three groups, according to the ending of the infinitive. The group tells you whether a verb is conjugated by a rule or whether you have to learn it by heart.

items.label: 1st group: *-er*
items.en: *parler, jouer, aimer*. About 9 verbs in 10, all regular (except *aller*).

items.label: 2nd group: *-ir* like *finir*
items.en: *finir, choisir, réussir*. Regular, with *-iss-* in the plural: *nous finissons*.

items.label: 3rd group: everything else
items.en: irregular verbs, which you learn in families

blocks.title: New verbs
blocks.en: Verbs that are added to the language are almost always in *-er*: *googler, liker, streamer*.

head: kind
what it means
example
rows: have the pronoun *se* and use *être* in the past

sections.title: Telling the group of an -ir verb

items.note: It has *-iss-*, so it is 2nd group.
No *-iss-*, so it is 3rd group. With *-ir* verbs you have to learn which is which.

items.en: The lesson ends at noon. (2nd group)

blocks.en: The **infinitive** is the basic form (*parler* = to speak). To conjugate, you cut off the ending and add an ending to the **stem** according to the person: *parl-er → je parl-e, nous parl-ons*.

Many endings are **written but not pronounced**. With *-er* verbs, *je parle, tu parles, il parle, ils parlent* sound identical. That is why the pronoun is compulsory, and why you learn the endings mainly for writing.
The ending *-ent* in the 3rd person plural of verbs is **always silent**: *ils parlent* sounds like *il parle*.

Tenses are **simple** (one word: *je parle, je parlais, je parlerai*) or **compound** (auxiliary + participle: *j'ai parlé*). Compound tenses are built on *avoir* and *être*, so you need to know those best.
About 9 in 10 French verbs end in *-er*, and they are conjugated completely regularly: cut off *-er* and add *-e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent*.
Only *-ons* and *-ez* are audible. The other endings are silent, so *je joue, tu joues, il joue, ils jouent* sound the same.
With verbs that begin with a vowel or a silent *h*, *je* shortens to *j'* and in the plural there is a liaison: *j'aime, nous‿aimons, ils‿aiment*.

blocks.title: Exception
blocks.en: *Aller* ends in *-er* but is completely irregular: *je vais, tu vas, il va...*

a: Est-ce que tu écoutes de la musique ?

blocks.en: Some *-er* verbs have regular endings, but their spelling changes inside the stem so that the pronunciation stays right.

head: type
what happens
example
rows: with *nous* the *e* stays, so *g* sounds soft
before a silent ending it becomes *è*
the consonant doubles before a silent ending

blocks.en: Without the *e*, *nous mangons* would be read with a hard *g*. Without *ç*, *nous commencons* would be read with a *k*.
The change happens only where the ending is **silent** (*je, tu, il, ils*). With *nous* and *vous* the stem stays as in the infinitive: *nous achetons, vous préférez*.
With *-yer*, the *y* becomes *i* before a silent ending. With *payer* both forms are correct: *je paie* and *je paye*.

checks.fr: Tu ___ le thé ou le café ?
checks.en: Do you prefer tea or coffee?

blocks.en: Verbs of the 2nd group end in *-ir* and have the insert *-iss-* in the plural. Endings: *-is, -is, -it, -issons, -issez, -issent*.
Many come from adjectives: *grand → grandir, gros → grossir, rouge → rougir*.

items.note: *Partir, sortir, dormir* end in *-ir* but do not have *-iss-*. They belong to the 3rd group.

items.fr: Le film finit à dix heures.

blocks.en: Regular verbs in **-re** (mostly **-dre**) drop *-re* and add **-s, -s, -, -ons, -ez, -ent**. In the *il / elle / on* form the stem stays alone (**il attend**), so the final *d* is silent but written. The past participle ends in **-u**.

head: verb
meaning
participle
rows: to defend, wait, spread, hold out

blocks.en: The **imparfait** is *j'attendais*, the **futur** *j'attendrai* (the *e* of *-re* is dropped, the *r* stays), the **conditionnel** *j'attendrais*, the **passé composé** *j'ai attendu*, the **imperative** *Attends ! Attendons ! Attendez !*, the **subjunctive** *que j'attende*.

items.en: I was waiting for the bus.

blocks.en: *Descendre*, *rendre*, *répondre* are regular, but **prendre** and **mettre** are not (*nous prenons, ils prennent*). See the irregular verbs.

items.fr: Nous attendons le train depuis vingt minutes.
items.en: We've been waiting for the train for twenty minutes.
She is selling her old guitar.

items.fr: Il ne répond jamais à mes messages.

checks.en: We are waiting for the bus.

blocks.en: A group of irregular **-ir** verbs drops the **last consonant of the stem** in the singular: *je pars, tu pars, il part* (but *nous partons*). The endings are **-s, -s, -t, -ons, -ez, -ent**. The past participle ends in **-i**, except *venir*-type verbs.
*Finir* adds **-iss-** in the plural (*nous finissons*). *Partir*, *sortir*, *dormir*, *servir*, *sentir* **do not**: *nous partons*, not *partissons*.

In the passé composé *partir* and *sortir* use **être** when they have no object: *Je suis parti. Elle est sortie.* *Sortir* with an object uses **avoir**: *J'ai sorti le chien.* *Dormir, servir, sentir, mentir* always take *avoir*.

items.fr: Elle est sortie avec ses amis.
items.en: She went out with her friends.

items.fr: Le serveur nous sert un café.
items.en: The waiter serves us a coffee.

checks.en: He sleeps ten hours a night.

Say it in the passé composé

blocks.en: These verbs end in **-ir** but are conjugated like **-er verbs** in the present: **-e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent**. The past participle is **-ert**: *ouvert, offert, couvert, découvert, souffert*.

head: verb
meaning
rows: to offer, give as a gift

blocks.en: The **futur** is *j'ouvrirai, j'offrirai*. The **imparfait** is *j'ouvrais, j'offrais*. The **imperative** has no *s* in *tu*: *Ouvre ! Offre !* The **passé composé** takes *avoir*: *J'ai ouvert, j'ai offert, j'ai découvert*.

items.fr: Ouvre la fenêtre, s'il te plaît.

blocks.en: *Offrir* is the verb for gifts: *offrir un cadeau à quelqu'un*. *Donner* is more general.

items.fr: Le magasin ouvre à neuf heures.
Nous avons découvert un petit village.

blocks.en: The four most important verbs in French. They are irregular, so you learn them by heart, and whole tenses are built on them: *avoir* and *être* form the passé composé, *aller* the near future.

head: verb
meaning

rows: weather and sports: *il fait beau, je fais du ski*

items.fr: Tu as des frères et sœurs ?
items.en: Do you have brothers and sisters?
They are going to the cinema.

items.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu fais ce soir ?

checks.en: What are you doing this weekend?

blocks.en: There are many irregular verbs, but they form **families with the same pattern**. If you know one, you know the whole family.
*Prendre*: *nous prenons*, but *ils prennent* (two *n*). *Venir*: *ils viennent*.
In the singular they lose the last consonant of the stem: *je pars, je sors, je dors*. In the plural they keep it: *nous partons, nous sortons, nous dormons*.

items.note: Only three verbs have the ending *-tes* with *vous*: *vous êtes, vous faites, vous dites*.

items.fr: Je prends le bus à sept heures.
items.en: I take the bus at seven.

checks.en: I sleep eight hours a night.

blocks.en: *Venir* and *tenir* have the stem **vien- / tien-** in the singular and the third person plural, **ven- / ten-** in *nous* and *vous*: *je viens, nous venons, ils viennent*. The participle is **venu** (with **être**) and **tenu** (with **avoir**). The whole family follows them.

The **futur** has a double *r*: *je viendrai, je tiendrai, nous deviendrons*. The **imparfait** is regular from *nous venons*: *je venais, je tenais*. The **subjunctive** is *que je vienne, que nous venions*.

items.fr: Je me souviens de ce jour.

blocks.en: *Venir de* + infinitive is the **recent past**: *Je viens de manger* (I have just eaten). *Venir de* + place is **origin**: *Je viens de Prague.* *Venir* + place without *de* is **to come to**: *Je viens à la fête.*

items.fr: Il tient son chien en laisse.
items.en: He's holding his dog on a lead.

checks.task_en: Say it in the passé composé

blocks.en: Verbs in **-aître** keep the **circumflex only before a t**: *il connaît* but *je connais, nous connaissons*. The stem gets **-ss-** in the plural. The participle is **-u**: *connu, paru, apparu*.

**Connaître** = to **know a person, a place, a thing** (you have met or been there): *Je connais Paul. Je connais Paris.* **Savoir** = to **know a fact or how to do something**: *Je sais nager. Je sais où il habite.* After *que*, *si*, *où*, *comment* use *savoir*.

items.fr: Le soleil a disparu derrière les nuages.
items.en: The sun disappeared behind the clouds.

checks.en: I've known Paul for a long time.

blocks.en: Four common irregular verbs with a **change of stem** between singular and plural. They have to be learned, but each follows a pattern: the **plural stem** appears in *nous* and *vous*, a **different stem** in *ils / elles*.

**Voir** and **croire** have **-y-** before a pronounced ending (*voyons, croyez*), and an *i* in the imparfait *nous voyions*. **Recevoir** gets a **cedilla** before *o* (*reçois, reçoit, reçoivent*, *reçu*) but not before *e* (*recevons*). The family: **apercevoir, décevoir, concevoir** (like recevoir), **prévoir** (like voir but *prévoirai*).

items.fr: Je vois un chat sur le toit.
items.en: I see a cat on the roof.

items.fr: Ils boivent du thé le matin.
items.en: They drink tea in the morning.
Do you get lots of messages?

blocks.en: *Croire à* (to believe in) takes **à**; *croire que* (to believe that) takes **que**: *Je crois à la chance. Je crois qu'il vient.* After a negative *croire* the subjunctive is common: *Je ne crois pas qu'il vienne.*

items.fr: Je ne vois rien sans mes lunettes.
items.en: I can't see anything without my glasses.

items.fr: Nous avons reçu une bonne nouvelle.

checks.en: She receives a lot of letters.

blocks.en: Five irregular verbs whose forms have to be learned. They share the **-s, -s, -t** endings of the singular and add **-s- or -v-** to the stem in the plural: *écrire → nous écrivons*, *lire → nous lisons*, *vivre → nous vivons*.
*Vous dites* (and *vous faites*) are the only *vous* forms that do not end in *-ez*.

items.fr: Je lis un livre par semaine.
items.en: I read a book a week.

items.fr: Je suis un cours de français.

blocks.en: *Je suis* is the **first person of être *and* of suivre**. The context tells you which: *Je suis fatigué* / *Je suis un cours*.

items.fr: Elle a écrit un long message.
Mes grands-parents ont vécu à Paris.

blocks.en: **Valoir** is mostly used in **il vaut mieux** + infinitive (*it's better to*): *Il vaut mieux partir tôt.* **Falloir** exists only as **il faut** (*il fallait, il faudra, il a fallu, qu'il faille*) and **pleuvoir** as *il pleut* (*il pleuvait, il pleuvra, il a plu*).

items.fr: Il a fallu beaucoup de temps.
items.en: It took a lot of time.

blocks.en: **Courir** has a double *r* in the future and conditional: *je courrai, je courrais*. **Mourir** too: *je mourrai*.

blocks.en: These four verbs combine with an **infinitive**, just like English "I can go, I want to sleep". All of them are irregular.

meaning

Je sais nager. Je sais où il habite.
can (I have the possibility, I'm allowed)

Je connais Paris. Je connais Léa.

items.note: *Je peux nager* means "I can go for a swim, I have the opportunity".

blocks.en: Instead of *je veux* (I want), you say politely *je voudrais* (I would like), and instead of *tu peux* it is nicer to say *tu pourrais* (could you).

items.fr: Je veux jouer aux jeux vidéo.
items.en: I want to play video games.
We have to do our homework.

items.fr: Je voudrais un croissant, s'il vous plaît.

articles.title: Obligation and necessity: devoir, il faut, avoir besoin de

blocks.en: To express **obligation** French has several tools. **Devoir** (*je dois*) is personal. **Il faut** is impersonal and general. **Avoir besoin de** says you need something. **Être obligé de** says you are forced to. Be careful with the **negative**: *il ne faut pas* means *you must not*, but *pas besoin de* means *you don't have to*.

sections.title: Il ne faut pas or pas besoin?

blocks.en: **Il ne faut pas** + infinitive = **prohibition** (*don't*). **Il n'est pas nécessaire de** and **ce n'est pas la peine de / pas besoin de** = **no need**. **Ne pas devoir** is also a prohibition: *Tu ne dois pas mentir.*

items.wrong: Tu n'as pas besoin de crier.
items.fr: Il [[ne faut pas]] crier. / Tu [[ne dois pas]] crier.
Tu [[n'as pas besoin de]] venir. / Ce [[n'est pas nécessaire]].

blocks.en: *Il faut* does not name who must. To name the person use a **pronoun before faut**: *Il **me** faut du temps* (I need time) or **il faut que + subjunctive**: *il faut que je parte*. With **an infinitive** it is general: *il faut manger pour vivre*.

items.fr: Il faut que tu fasses tes devoirs.
items.en: You have to do your homework.

items.fr: Il faut dix minutes pour y aller.
items.en: It takes ten minutes to get there.
You have to eat to live.

blocks.en: *Devoir* + infinitive means **must** (obligation), **probably** (*Il doit être malade*) and **to be supposed to** (*Le train doit arriver à huit heures*). *Devoir* + noun means **to owe**: *Je te dois dix euros.*

items.fr: Nous devons partir à huit heures.
items.en: We are to leave at eight.

items.fr: Il faut que je finisse mon devoir avant ce soir.
items.en: I have to finish my homework before tonight.

items.fr: Tu n'as pas besoin de venir.
Il ne faut pas courir près de la piscine.
items.en: You mustn't run near the pool.

a: Tu n'as pas besoin de venir.
Il n'est pas nécessaire de venir.
Ce n'est pas nécessaire de venir.

checks.fr: Il ___ que tu fasses tes devoirs.
checks.en: You have to do your homework.

blocks.en: A reflexive verb has a pronoun before it that **changes with the person**: *je me lève, tu te lèves*. In the past it always uses *être*: *je me suis levé*.

items.fr: Je me réveille à six heures et demie.
items.en: I wake up at half past six.
Do you go to bed late?

items.fr: On se retrouve devant le cinéma.
items.en: We'll meet in front of the cinema.

checks.en: I go to bed at ten.

a: Je ne me lève pas tôt.

articles.title: Reflexive verbs in every tense and mood

blocks.en: A reflexive verb always has its **pronoun** (*me, te, se, nous, vous, se*) right before the verb. In **compound tenses** it uses **être** and the participle agrees with the pronoun if it is a **direct** object. The pronoun follows a **positive command** (*Lève-toi !*) and goes before the **infinitive** (*Je vais me lever.*).

head: form
example
English
rows: Do you get up? / Did you get up?

blocks.en: Auxiliary **être**: *je me suis lavé(e), tu t'es lavé(e), il s'est lavé, elle s'est lavée, nous nous sommes lavé(e)s*. The participle **agrees with the subject** if the pronoun is a **direct** object. It does **not** agree when there is another direct object (*Elle s'est lavé **les mains***) or when the pronoun is indirect (*Elles se sont téléphoné*).

items.note: The hands are the direct object, so no agreement.

blocks.en: *Se* with a **plural subject** can mean **each other**: *Ils s'aiment, nous nous écrivons, elles se parlent.* It is the same form as the reflexive; the context tells which meaning.

items.fr: Ils se voient tous les week-ends.
items.en: They see each other every weekend.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes rencontrés à Paris.
Les deux amis se téléphonent souvent.
items.en: The two friends often phone each other.

sections.title: Verbs that are reflexive only in French

blocks.en: Many verbs are reflexive in French but not in English: **se souvenir de** (to remember), **s'en aller** (to leave), **se passer** (to happen), **se tromper** (to be wrong), **s'asseoir** (to sit down), **se dépêcher** (to hurry), **se promener** (to take a walk), **s'ennuyer** (to be bored), **se débrouiller** (to manage).

items.fr: Dépêche-toi, on va être en retard !
items.en: Hurry up, we're going to be late!

items.fr: Je me suis trompé de numéro.
Elle s'est fait mal au pied.
Je me suis réveillé à sept heures.

checks.task_en: Say it in the passé composé
Say it in the passé composé

checks.en: I'm going to get up early.

blocks.en: When two verbs follow each other, only the **first** is conjugated and the second stays in the infinitive. Between them there is either nothing, *à*, or *de*, depending on the first verb.

head: construction
verbs
example
rows: aimer, adorer, détester, préférer, vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, savoir, aller
commencer à, apprendre à, aider à, réussir à
arrêter de, essayer de, oublier de, décider de, finir de

items.note: The second verb stays in the infinitive.

blocks.en: Learn the construction together with the verb: not *essayer*, but *essayer de*.

items.fr: N'oublie pas de fermer la porte.
items.en: Don't forget to close the door.

items.fr: Tu m'aides à porter le sac ?
items.en: Will you help me carry the bag?

checks.en: I'm learning to play the guitar.
My sister is starting to talk.

articles.title: Verbs followed by à, de or nothing + infinitive

blocks.en: When two verbs follow each other, the second is an **infinitive**, linked in one of **three ways**: **directly**, with **à** or with **de**. There is no rule, but the groups are stable, so learn the verb with its link.

head: link
typical verbs
example
rows: aimer, adorer, détester, préférer, vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, savoir, aller, désirer, falloir, espérer, penser, venir
commencer à, continuer à, apprendre à, réussir à, hésiter à, aider à, se mettre à, arriver à, passer du temps à
finir de, arrêter de, essayer de, décider de, oublier de, refuser de, avoir envie de, avoir peur de, avoir besoin de, demander de, promettre de, conseiller de

blocks.en: *Aimer, vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, savoir, aller, espérer, préférer, désirer, détester* and the verbs of motion take **no preposition**. A pronoun goes before the infinitive: *Je veux le voir.*
**À** goes with **beginning, continuing, learning, succeeding and helping**.
**De** goes with **ending, trying, deciding, forgetting, refusing** and the expressions with **avoir** (*avoir envie de, besoin de, peur de, l'intention de*).

Some verbs change meaning with their link. **Demander à qqn de** + infinitive: *Je lui demande de venir.* **Dire à qqn de**: *Elle me dit de partir.* **Commencer par** + infinitive means *to begin by*; **finir par** means *to end up*: *Il a fini par comprendre.*

items.fr: Tu as réussi à ouvrir la porte ?
items.en: Did you manage to open the door?

items.fr: Elle a peur de parler en public.
items.en: She is afraid of speaking in public.

articles.title: The infinitive: avant de, sans, pour, après avoir

blocks.en: The infinitive is used **after prepositions** (*pour, sans, avant de, au lieu de, afin de*), as a **noun** (*Lire est agréable*), after **modals and verbs of wanting** (*je veux partir*) and in **instructions** (*Ajouter du sel*). Its **negative** goes in front together: **ne pas** + infinitive.

head: use
example
English
rows: Je travaille pour gagner de l'argent.
Il part sans dire au revoir.
Lave-toi les mains avant de manger.
Il demande de ne pas parler.
He asks us not to speak.

blocks.en: To say that the action was **finished before** the main verb use **avoir or être + past participle**: *après avoir mangé, après être arrivé(e)*. With *être* verbs and reflexives the participle agrees with the subject: *Après être arrivée, elle a téléphoné.* Both actions must have **the same subject**.

items.fr: Après avoir fini, il est parti.
Après être rentrés, ils ont dîné.
items.en: After coming home they had dinner.

items.fr: Après s'être lavée, elle a mangé.

blocks.en: With *avant de, après, sans, pour* the infinitive needs the **same subject** as the main verb. With different subjects use a clause: *avant que* + subjunctive, *pour que* + subjunctive, *sans que* + subjunctive.

items.fr: Il est sorti sans prendre son manteau.
items.en: He went out without taking his coat.

items.fr: Fermez la porte avant de partir.
Il vaut mieux ne pas attendre.

a: Il part sans dire au revoir.
Lave-toi les mains avant de manger.
Lavez-vous les mains avant de manger.
Après être arrivée, elle a téléphoné.

checks.en: He asks us not to speak.

blocks.en: **Faire + infinitive** means to **cause** something to happen or to **have it done**: *Je fais réparer ma voiture* (I'm having my car repaired). **Laisser + infinitive** means **to let**: *Je laisse partir les enfants.* **Voir, entendre, regarder, écouter + infinitive** say **what you perceive**: *Je vois venir le bus.*

head: structure
example
English
rows: Il fait rire tout le monde.
Elle se fait couper les cheveux.

blocks.en: The two verbs form a **block**: nothing goes in between and a pronoun goes before *faire*: *Je le fais réparer.* *Faire* is an auxiliary-like verb, so in the passé composé the participle **fait** never agrees: *Je les ai fait venir.*

items.fr: Nous avons fait construire une maison.

blocks.en: With **laisser** and the verbs of **perception** a pronoun goes before the first verb: *Je les vois jouer.* *Laisse-le faire.* The participle of *laisser* can stay unchanged.

items.fr: Elle laisse son fils jouer dehors.
items.en: She lets her son play outside.
We watch the cars go by.

items.fr: Il fait toujours rire ses amis.
items.en: He always makes his friends laugh.

a: Il fait rire tout le monde.

blocks.en: French and English (and Czech) verbs often take a different preposition or case. Learn the ones that differ together with their construction.

items.fr: Je me souviens de ce jour.

articles.title: Expressions with avoir and faire
articles.fr: les expressions avec avoir et faire

blocks.en: Where English and Czech say "I'm cold, I'm afraid", French **has**: *j'ai froid, j'ai peur*. And French expresses many activities and the weather with the verb *faire*.

head: avoir...
English
rows: to be right, to be wrong
to hurt, to have a pain in

blocks.en: *Avoir mal à* + a part of the body: *J'ai mal à la tête* (I have a headache), *j'ai mal au ventre* (my stomach hurts), *j'ai mal aux dents* (my teeth hurt).

head: faire...
English
rows: faire du sport, du vélo, du ski
to do sport, to cycle, to ski
il fait beau, il fait froid
the weather is nice, it's cold
to pay attention, to be careful

blocks.en: *Je fais du sport* (I do sport), but *je joue au foot* (I play football). Ball games and games: *jouer à*. Other sports: *faire de*.

items.note: For the weather: *il fait froid*. For how you feel: *j'ai froid*.

items.fr: Le week-end, je fais du vélo.

blocks.en: The passive is formed with *être* + the past participle. The participle agrees with the subject. Who does the action is introduced by *par*.

items.en: Victor Hugo wrote this book. → This book was written by Victor Hugo.
items.fr: Victor Hugo a écrit ce livre. → Ce livre [[a été écrit]] [[par]] Victor Hugo.

rows.en: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889.

sections.title: The tense is carried by être

head: tense
example
rows: Le match est diffusé à la télé.
Le match a été diffusé à la télé.
Le match sera diffusé à la télé.

blocks.en: In everyday speech French avoids the passive and uses *on*. At B1 it is enough to **recognise** the passive in a text and to form a simple one.

items.note: More natural than *Le français est parlé ici.*
